entry.title: 0% GPU utilization: How SANSAR hides Linux cryptomining
entry.content:
red-team · rootkit

SANSAR is a Linux cryptomining orchestrator targeting GPU systems that operates command-and-control infrastructure over Tor while deploying a kernel rootkit, GPU hooks, and an Ethereum-based backdoor for C2 retrieval. The malware actively demonstrates sophisticated evasion techniques including 0% GPU utilization masking and kernel-level persistence, indicating moderate-to-high severity with evidence of active exploitation in the wild. Affected systems are Linux servers and workstations with GPUs; immediate actions include kernel patching, implementing rootkit detection tools, network segmentation to restrict Tor egress, and GPU process monitoring for anomalous activity. Organizations should audit systems for unexpected kernel modules and cryptocurrency mining processes, with priority given to internet-facing or compromised Linux infrastructure.

The flaw requires two specially crafted requests and only triggers when a compromised server assumes primary role, creating a window for exploitation during cluster rebalancing. Severity is high given the pre-auth requirement and potential for widespread replica set outages; active exploitation status unclear. Patch immediately to the fixed versions released by MongoDB this week for all affected replica set members.

entry.title: node-opcua: Namespace-Level RBAC Fail-Open - Anonymous Write/Call Bypass via Unbound `DefaultRolePermissions (CVE-2026-95860)
entry.content:
vulnerability · auth-bypass · CVE-2026-95860

node-opcua and related packages (node-opcua-address-space, node-opcua-server) fail to enforce role-based access control (RBAC) at the namespace level, allowing unauthenticated clients to write protected variables and call privileged methods on nodes lacking explicit per-node permissions. The vulnerability stems from improper handling of DefaultRolePermissions inheritance; the implementation grants access instead of applying the required default-deny policy specified in OPC UA Part 3. Severity is critical with no indication of active exploitation reported. Immediately patch to the latest version and review OPC UA server configurations to ensure explicit RolePermissions are defined on sensitive nodes as a temporary mitigation.

Read more · Source: github-advisories

entry.title: bitcoinjs-lib: Undetected merkle node duplication in block root computation validates a forged transaction list (CVE-2026-107846)
entry.content:
vulnerability · merkle-tree-collision · CVE-2026-107846

The bitcoinjs-lib npm package contains a critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-107846) in its merkle root computation where `fastMerkleRoot` silently pads odd-level nodes by self-hashing without indication, allowing attackers to duplicate transactions while maintaining an identical merkle root and block hash. This enables forged transaction lists to pass validation since `checkTxRoots` does not detect repeated transactions, and the block header retains valid proof-of-work. There is no indication of active wild exploitation. Affected applications should immediately update bitcoinjs-lib to a patched version that properly detects and rejects duplicate transactions in merkle tree construction.

entry.content:
vulnerability · parser-differential · CVE-2026-115905

The Rust `zip` crate (versions ≤9.0.4) contains a critical parser differential vulnerability (CVE-2026-115905) where `ZipArchive` and `ZipStreamReader` interpret filenames differently—the former trusts the Central Directory File Header while the latter relies on the Local File Header. Attackers can craft malicious ZIP archives with inconsistent headers to achieve arbitrary file overwrites and remote code execution, exploiting this inconsistency to bypass security controls. This vulnerability is critical severity; no active exploitation in the wild has been confirmed at time of advisory. Immediately update to `zip` version >9.0.4 and validate all ZIP extraction logic, particularly any code using `ZipStreamReader`.

entry.title: Linux Kernel: Linux Kernel Missing Initialization of a Variable Vulnerability (CVE-2026-46300)
entry.content:
vulnerability · uninitialized-variable · CVE-2026-46300, CVE-2026-98432

The Linux Kernel contains a missing variable initialization vulnerability (CVE-2026-46300) affecting ESP input processing during socket buffer coalescing, allowing unintended modification of page-cache-backed data and decryption of shared fragments in place. This vulnerability is actively exploited in the wild and can be chained with CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to achieve remote code execution as root, including PHP webshell implantation. Immediately apply kernel security updates per vendor instructions and CISA BOD 26-04 prioritization guidance; affected systems should be patched without delay given active exploitation. If patches are unavailable, discontinue use of the affected kernel versions and perform forensic triage per CISA requirements.

entry.title: Critical 16-Year-Old UEFI Flaw Can Run Code Before Secure Boot on Network-Booting Servers
entry.content:
vulnerability · rce

EDK II UEFI firmware contains a critical remote code execution vulnerability in network boot (PXE) functionality that enables attackers to execute code before Secure Boot validation. The flaw, present for 16 years, allows unauthenticated code execution during network boot sequences on affected servers. This vulnerability has high severity and is exploited in the wild; it requires network-level access and affects systems configured for network booting. Hardware vendors using EDK II must immediately patch affected UEFI implementations, and organizations should disable network boot by default, restrict PXE boot access to trusted networks only, and validate boot images cryptographically where possible.

entry.title: Researcher Reveals How Logic Bugs Alone Cracked Microsoft Edge in $175,000 Pwn2Own Win
entry.content:
vulnerability · logic-bug,sandbox-escape

Microsoft Edge was compromised through a chain of logic bugs without requiring memory corruption vulnerabilities, enabling arbitrary code execution outside the sandbox when a user visits a malicious webpage. The attack chain, disclosed by Orange Tsai after a five-month embargo, exploited design flaws rather than traditional memory safety issues and earned $175,000 at Pwn2Own Berlin in May 2024. Microsoft patched the vulnerabilities immediately following the contest, though the specific severity rating and current exploitation status in the wild are not detailed. Security engineers should ensure Edge is fully updated and review the disclosed logic flaw patterns to identify similar design weaknesses in other browser isolation mechanisms.

entry.content:

Volt Typhoon deployed Silent Train, a covert network leveraging compromised SOHO/IoT/enterprise infrastructure with rotating chains for persistent access and zero-day exploitation across four campaigns since late 2023. The group exploited multiple zero-day vulnerabilities to establish strategic footholds in critical infrastructure, representing high severity threats with active exploitation confirmed. Network defenders should prioritize identifying and isolating compromised edge devices, implement strict egress filtering on SOHO/IoT devices, deploy behavioral analytics for detecting rotating command-and-control chains, and ensure rapid patching of zero-day disclosures. Organizations in critical infrastructure sectors should conduct forensic reviews for Silent Train indicators and coordinate with CISA for threat intelligence regarding affected systems.

entry.title: eMudhra-TLS-Leck: Apple lässt Problem auf macOS-Kommandozeile zunächst bestehen
entry.content:
vulnerability · cert-validation

eMudhra certificate authority issued a fraudulent TLS certificate that was included in macOS system certificate bundles used by command-line tools, creating a trusted path for potential man-in-the-middle attacks. Apple has patched browsers but left the legacy cert.pem file used by CLI utilities unpatched, exposing developers and administrators using command-line tools to ongoing risk. Users should manually remove the compromised eMudhra certificate from the system cert.pem file or update to the latest macOS version when available, and review any TLS traffic from CLI tools for signs of compromise.
